I’ve been farming these lands in Quzhou County for over thirty years now. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land, and at 52, I’ve seen enough good years and bad years to know what works. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension technician tells me, but at the end of the day, I trust my own eyes and what the neighbors are doing more than any book.

This year, I’m sticking with the wheat-maize double crop on all 10 mu. It’s the safest bet around here—everyone in my village does it, and if one crop has a bad year, the other usually pulls us through. I thought about planting a few mu of cotton like some folks down south in the county, but cotton prices have been up and down, and I don’t have the labor for all that hand-picking. My wife and I can handle the wheat and maize ourselves, with some hired help at harvest.

For the winter wheat, I’ll plant in mid-October. I’m buying improved wheat seed again—maybe Jimai or something similar from the seed shop. I used to save my own seed, but the bought seed gives me 50–100 jin more per mu, so it pays for itself. I’ll rotary till before planting, put down about 120 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and topdress with another 50 jin or so at jointing. The extension guy told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually put down closer to 16–17 kg because I’d rather waste a little money than risk a bad yield. I’ll irrigate four times: once before winter, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at filling. Water costs money, but without it, you get nothing. I’ll spray pesticides three or four times—herbicide once, insecticide two or three times depending on what I see in the field. If the year is normal, I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, I’ll plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June. There’s no time for tillage—everyone here does no-till maize planting right into the wheat stubble. I’ll buy hybrid seed, probably a Nongda or Denghai variety. I’ll put down compound fertilizer at planting and maybe topdress once if the plants look yellow. I irrigate twice for maize—once right after planting if it’s dry, and once at the big喇叭口 stage. That’s usually enough. Pesticide-wise, I spray three times. I’m hoping for 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.
